gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noticia-text: Wide-mouthed capitals barely taller than the lowercase lead in Azonix. Noticia Text follows with a dignified text serif, big curved entrances and tall small letters, so long paragraphs feel literary and settled beneath that rigid, pen-drawn heading.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla has a refined serif body whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, and its e opens like a pried clasp. And Azonix, bent from a single wire-like line, commands the headline while Piazzolla does the patient work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-pridi: Pridi reads as a classic, refined text serif, with generous gaps where its curves meet the stems and small letters standing nearly capital-sized. Azonix, rounded-rod and single-weight, sits above it nicely.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-scope-one: Scope One reads traditional and refined, its counters spilling out into the space around them. Beside the identical-weight strokes of Azonix, its stubby ascenders and big x-height give the pairing a sturdy, easygoing grip on the page.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px brings a bookish, dignified text serif with large open counters in its tall a, e and s. Under Azonix, whose strokes are as stout as drawn pipe cleaner, Slabo 13px lets the heading's severity ease into clear, legible rounded forms.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum opens with a c as open as a bent paperclip, and its serif x-height rises high like a squared-off woodblock letter. Azonix, cut like laser sheet at one stroke width, is the blunt headline voice; Suwannaphum does the editorial talking.
gen-dafont-azonix-instrument-sans: Crisp, modern and wide-mouthed, Azonix up top meets Instrument Sans, whose c ends point apart like open pincers and whose strokes never vary. Paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-azonix-inter: Azonix is startling for how its capitals barely rise above the lowercase, so words need a moment to knit back together. Inter, a plain sans with breathing counters and a smooth tube-like line, supplies a steady, quiet counterpoint.
gen-dafont-azonix-mulish: Sharp, wide and unmistakably authoritative, Azonix takes the top spot with crisp letters that hold up even when shrunk. Mulish, in turn, is modern and approachable, with horseshoe-open apertures, a large x-height and short ascenders.
gen-dafont-blockletter-bitter: Precise, with a tall midsection and pencil-even lines, Blockletter holds the top as a display voice drawn like a steady line of toothpaste. Bitter, a slab-serif, brings grounded, dependable lowercase with a huge eye and an s you can see through.
